title: Polynomial-time production of native trajectories
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over Booleans, let $y$ and $T$ be functions from Boolean words to Boolean words and to natural numbers, respectively. If both $y$ and the function sending $x$ to the unary word of length $T(x)$ are polynomial-time computable, then the function sending $x$ to the serialized trajectory of $M$ on input $y(x)$ through time $T(x)$ inclusive is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over Booleans
$y$ maps Boolean words to Boolean words
$T$ maps Boolean words to natural numbers
the function mapping $x$ to the unary word of length $T(x)$ is polynomial-time computable
replaced: If a reference-input producer and a unary-horizon producer are polynomial-time computable, then the function sending an input $x$ to the inclusive serialized trajectory of the source over the produced reference input, with the produced horizon plus one rows, is polynomial-time computable; no recomputed semantics or unbounded numeric conversion is used.
